name: Rosewood AMAALA
positioning: Wellness-focused Red Sea resort between desert and sea, with private-pool pavilions, suites, villas and lodges
best_for: Travelers seeking a wellness retreat with spa rituals and breathwork
Families or groups wanting multi-bedroom villas with private pools

facts.text: The resort rests between the desert terrain and the open water of the Red Sea.
The coastline has coral gardens and clear waters.
At Asaya, sea-inspired therapies use the composition of the Red Sea water.
Guided breathwork and soundbath experiences are offered, and there is a daily Sukun Hour, a shared moment of stillness for reflection.
Olea serves Mediterranean cuisine celebrating seasonal produce and olive oil.
The Grill Bar & Restaurant does live-fire cooking over wood and charcoal.
Asaya Lounge serves conscious cuisine and botanical beverages.
Private, residential-style dining is available inside your villa or at curated gathering spaces.
Suites have separate living areas and private pools.
The Sea View Private Pool Pavilion has two queen beds and sleeps up to 4 guests.
The Two Bedroom Private Pool Villas have a king bed and two queen beds, sleep up to 5 guests, and have a pool and whirlpool.

highlights.text: At the Arabian Apothecary at Asaya, guests create bespoke healing blends from regional botanical oils and herbs.
Activities include swim rituals in circulation pools, via ferrata in the Hijazi Mountains, al fresco dining along the reef and yachting at dusk.
The Asaya Lodge with Private Pool is a one-bedroom retreat within Asaya with a private treatment room set around a garden terrace.
Saha serves progressive Middle Eastern cuisine in intimate pavilion-style settings, and Puro Cove Club offers relaxed coastal dining with ceviches and crudos.
Villas come in one-, two- and three-bedroom configurations, with expansive terraces and private pools.

considerations.text: The resort is a two-hour drive from Red Sea International Airport; transfers are arranged in private Red Sea electric vehicles, or guests can arrive via the marina by boat.
WhataHotel notes that the resort sits within a developing destination where surrounding amenities are still expanding.
